A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPM/GPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A–F are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V2 reports original cyclic-preference, RewardBench, AlpacaEval, and MT-Bench results, including ablations and LN-GPO experiments in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–7, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix E.2 generalizes the existing LN-GPO objective from normalization by |y| to |y|^gamma, introducing an adjustable exponent. V3 specifies gamma = 1 for the unchanged Table 7 results. The core GPM architecture and GPO update remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same Skywork training data, Ultrafeedback-derived cyclic datasets, RewardBench tasks, and downstream alignment benchmarks remain. The expanded cyclic-dataset construction instructions describe existing coverage rather than an added dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–7 retain the same evaluated comparators, including BT reward models and SPPO/GPO configurations. Newly discussed methods such as ArmoRM appear in related work, not as added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, model settings, evaluation procedures, and metrics remain unchanged; Tables 8–9 match exactly. Gemma-2-9B-it training details remain in Appendix E.3 despite removal of its result paragraph. Newly supplied construction and metric details do not establish changed protocols.

E4.justification: The embedding-dimension, scale-gate, and L2-normalization ablations, Figure 3 cyclic visualizations, LN-GPO comparison, and Appendix F examples are retained. The new length-control discussion interprets existing evidence rather than adding an ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3 does not introduce uncertainty estimation or statistical reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 are unchanged. V3 removes Section 6.1's prose-only Gemma-2-9B-it results, including average RewardBench scores of 92.33% for GPM versus 91.46% for BT and the associated Chat and Chat-Hard scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 explicitly connects the learning rate through eta = 1/beta and adds bounded eigenvalues alongside normalized embeddings as a rationale for the bounded-score premise. This modestly extends the theoretical justification; theorem statements and displayed proof calculations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about expressive preference embeddings, linear query complexity, modeling cyclic preferences, and preference-score-based alignment with GPO.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 newly discusses how longer GPM responses can improve raw win rate while hurting length-controlled win rate. It proposes a mechanism involving comprehensive answers, identifies conciseness-sensitive applications, and acknowledges that the retained LN-GPO results leave further length-control tuning necessary.

D1.justification: V3 adds stepwise cyclic-dataset filtering and pair-label construction instructions, identifies the final hidden state as the embedding source, and expands Table 3's metric, reference-model, and length-unit explanations. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: Appendix D adds citations to Bengio, Wang's ArmoRM work, Mitchell, Liang, and Furuta. It provides focused comparisons with multidimensional reward models and noisy/soft-preference optimization while retaining the established expressiveness and efficiency positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact. V3 promotes and renames the pair-preference subsection, adds Impact Statement and Acknowledgements sections, updates author information, and makes localized explanatory and appendix rewrites.

P2.justification: V3 converts the main text and references to a two-column conference layout, changes typography and table sizing, and extensively reflows figures and appendices. All three figures and nine tables remain, with expanded Figure 2 and Table 3 captions. Figure 2's new left/right wording mismatches its vertically stacked examples.

improvement.justification: The added construction instructions, implementation explanations, and explicit length-bias discussion modestly improve reproducibility and interpretation. These gains outweigh the limited loss of the prose-only Gemma-2-9B-it results and the small Figure 2 caption defect. The experimental tables and core proof calculations remain unchanged, so the improvement chiefly concerns documentation and qualification of existing evidence.
